title: Compatibility layer: embeddings/rerank semantic contract, pagination, and retry playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a compatibility layer that ensures parity between legacy embeddings/rerank clients and the new unified embeddings+reranker endpoints. The adapter must normalize pagination semantics, unify HTTP error codes for idempotent retry behavior, and preserve structured output (scores, metadata, provenance) for customers using older SDKs. This ticket defines the semantic mapping, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and monitoring needed to reduce migration friction and prevent regressions.
background_and_problem_statement: Across inbound customer reports and internal telemetry we see a class of failures when customers upgrade runtime or route through the new unified embeddings endpoint. Root causes: (1) legacy clients expect page-style cursors and Link headers while new endpoints prefer opaque tokens; (2) inconsistent HTTP 4xx/5xx mapping leads to unsafe retries; (3) some clients expect per-item structured metadata fields (source_id, chunk_id, score) that changed shape in the new response. Result: failed pagination, duplicated requests, and downstream ranking errors in customer systems.
proposal_summary:
Build a compatibility adapter deployed at the API gateway layer that performs:
- Cursor normalization: accept legacy `cursor` query param and translate to opaque `page_token`, and generate Link headers for legacy clients.
- Error normalization: map internal errors to a stable set of canonical HTTP codes and machine-readable error bodies; include `retryable: true|false` in JSON errors.
- Structured output preservation: emit legacy-style `items[]` with `id`, `embedding`, `score`, and top-level `next_cursor` while preserving the new richer `result_set_v2` as an alternate key.
- Idempotency helper: accept `Idempotency-Key` and ensure at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics are documented and configurable per-customer.
The adapter should be feature-flagged per-tenant and deployed behind the unified endpoint so that clients do not need code changes immediately.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Legacy SDKs (v1.x) can call `/v1/embeddings/rerank` with `cursor` and receive a Link header + `next_cursor` behavior identical to old endpoint (pagination ordering preserved).
2) Error bodies include `code`, `message`, and `retryable` fields; mapping doc exists and automated tests assert mappings for 30 canonical errors.
3) Structured item fields retain `source_id`, `chunk_id`, and `score` keys for backward compatibility; samples exist in test corpus verifying parsing by legacy clients.
4) Under a 30% traffic canary, telemetry shows no degradation in p99 latency > 15% of baseline and no increase in 5xx rate above 0.1% absolute.
5) Rollout plan executed with feature-flag toggles and a documented rollback path.
non_goals: Do not change the new unified contract for new clients. This ticket is an adapter and operational playbook only. We're not deprecating old clients in this work.
semantic_mapping_and_edge_cases:
- Cursor translation: adapter must map legacy cursor offsets to v2 tokens; for very large offsets use offset+token hybrid to avoid O(N) paging.
- Sorting/ordering: preserve sort stability for top-k deterministic rerank. Add integration tests with seeded RNG.
- Partial failures: if one shard fails, return partial results plus `partial: true` and `retryable: true` when safe.
- Empty pages: unify `next_cursor` to empty string and Link header absence for EOF.
- Idempotency collisions: collision resolution policy documented; when `Idempotency-Key` reused with different payload return 409 with `retryable:false`.
monitoring_and_slo: New metrics to add: `compat_adapter.request_count`, `compat_adapter.error_rate`, `compat_adapter.cursor_mismatch_rate`, `compat_adapter.retryable_error_rate`, and `compat_adapter.latency_p99`. Alerting: fire pager if `compat_adapter.error_rate > 0.5%` sustained 5m or if `cursor_mismatch_rate > 0.1%`. SLO: keep additional p99 latency introduced by adapter < 15ms for 95% of requests.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement adapter behind feature flag in staging; unit + integration tests validate mappings.
2) Canary: enable for 1% of traffic for a single low-latency region for 48h.
3) Expand to 10% across two regions for 72h; monitor metrics and customer support slack channel.
4) 30% canary for 7 days with opt-in customers (notify via admin console).
5) Gradual ramp to 100% with weekly checkpoints; if any alert thresholds hit, rollback to previous flag.
Rollback: flip feature flag off; the adapter logs will include request ids for postmortem lookup.
qa_plan:
- Create synthetic legacy client harness that runs full pagination traversal and validates ordering and metadata preservation.
- Add fuzz tests for cursors and malformed tokens.
- E2E tests exercising Idempotency-Key collisions and partial-shard failures.
- Manual verification with 3 pilot customers (Prod-like datasets) and capture parsing logs.
- Post-deploy smoke test triggered by CI after toggling feature flag.
security_and_compliance_considerations: Adapter must not log or persist raw embeddings. All telemetry fields must be hashed or sampled; sensitive metadata redaction enforced. Ensure compatibility layer honors tenant KMS settings and audit logs remain unchanged. Security reviewed for information exposure risk if we surface original error reasons; only include high-level error categories in public response.
open_questions_and_decisions_needed:
1) Do we expose `retryable` boolean in stable public API or confine to compatibility responses? (PM decision required)
2) How long to support adapter as default behavior for new tenants? Suggested: 12 months with deprecation notices.
3) Should adapter attempt transparent replays to construct legacy cursors for non-idempotent operations? (Ops risk)
Decision log: provisional: expose `retryable` in compat responses only; deprecation timeline set to 12 months.
communication_and_customer_migration:
- Draft customer-facing migration guide explaining cursor/token differences, recommended client library updates, and the deprecation timeline.
- Post status pages during canary phases and dedicate Solutions Eng office hours for the first 2 weeks of 30% canary.
- Notify top-50 customers directly with migration checklist and SDK patches.
